D See the use of some more transitive verbs in the following sentences:

(i) Who has broken the cup?

(ii) He reads a lot of story books.

(iii) I shall take a cup of tea now.

Now use the following verbs as transitive in your own sentences :

kill, prey, sell, draw, learn

E Here are some more example of intransitive verbs.

(i) The baby is sleeping.

(ii) Boys are playing in the field.

(iii) He was killed in an accident.

Note: An intransitive verb may be followed by nothing or it may be followed by any number of adverbials.

Now use the following verbs as intransitive in your own sentences :

walk $\quad\quad\quad$ work $\quad\quad\quad$ die $\quad\quad\quad$ laugh $\quad\quad\quad$ open

Remember, the same verb may be used as linking, transitive or intransitive. It depends on how you use it.

For example:

He ran home. (intransitive)

The river runs dry in summer. (linking)

I ran a race. (transitive)

Can you think of any other verb like this? Use it in 3 different ways.
